_readme: US-1997 AC4: the SHARED behavioural fixture for the category grading rubrics.
There are two rubric definitions — services/edge-functions/src/lib/rubric.ts (server
source of truth, carries prompt guidance + defect routing) and src/lib/rubrics.ts (client,
renders the certificate Factor Breakdown) — because the edge and the web app are separate
projects that cannot import each other. They are declared to stay in sync (factor keys +
weights + labels) and NOTHING pinned them, so a divergence would silently render a cert
against weights the grade was never computed on.
The guard is the SAME remedy US-1995 used for title-sync: both suites load this file and
assert their RUBRICS match it exactly. Change a rubric's factors/labels/weights HERE first,
then in both rubric modules — never in one module alone.
This file constrains ONLY key + label + weight (the fields both sides share). The server's
extra fields (guidance, promptGuidance, defectRouting) are not mirrored on the client and
are out of scope for the parity check.
_weighted_readme: US-1997 activation step 2: the SCORING half of the parity guard.
The block above pins the rubric DEFINITIONS. This block pins what both mirrors DO with
them — computeRubricWeightedOverall, the generalized weighted overall that replaces the
clothing-only FACTOR_WEIGHTS loops in ai-grading.ts and human-review.ts for any rubric.
Definitions matching while the arithmetic drifts would leave a cert rendering the right
factor labels against a number computed some other way, which is the failure this whole
Every expected_overall here was derived by hand from the weights, NOT captured from a
run — a fixture recorded from the implementation it tests only pins the bug in place.
Cases avoid exact .05 boundaries so float noise cannot flip a round-half-up tie and make
the suites disagree for a reason that has nothing to do with drift.
watches and shoes share clothing's .30/.25/.20/.15/.10 vector, so their cases reuse sums
already verified by weighted-grade-cases.json. sports_cards (.30/.25/.25/.20) is the only
novel weight vector and carries the arithmetic in its own right.
_refusal_readme: Inputs on which BOTH mirrors must THROW rather than return a number, with the SAME message.
Same rule and the same reasoning as weighted-grade-cases.json refusal_cases (US-2386): a
missing factor scored as 0 produces a plausible low grade that nothing flags, and the
certificate reseal then certifies it. With a variable factor set the risk is strictly
higher, because 'which factors did this rubric expect' is no longer obvious from the code,
so the message names the rubric too.
Same two JSON encoding limits as that fixture: undefined cannot be written (the key is
simply dropped), and NaN is carried as the sentinel string "__NaN__", which each runner
MUST convert to a real NaN before calling. A runner that forgets asserts on a string, which
also throws — so the test would pass for the wrong reason. Assert the sentinel is translated.

refusal_cases.why: surface omitted — the heaviest sports_cards factor at 30%
centering omitted — the lightest, so a coalesced result would be closest to plausible
explicit null, which is what a partially-populated factor_scores JSONB yields
NaN (sentinel) — arithmetic already went wrong upstream; do not launder it into a grade
a numeric-looking string — JS would coerce it in the multiply and return a real-looking overall
clothing scores handed to the sports_cards rubric — a mis-routed report, not a missing value. Every expected key is absent, so it must refuse rather than score a card on zero factors
